_comment: Evidence for the one-time reconcile of jobs held by the channel-loss bug. See
scripts/reconcile_channel_loss.py. Every entry under `confirmed` is a held job whose
submit reached the ATS: the company sent a confirmation email within roughly a minute
of the hold timestamp. Entries under `not_confirmed` stay held, because the only mail
they produced is a Greenhouse security code and no confirmation ever followed.
The two True Anomaly confirmations do not name the role, so they are paired with the
two held True Anomaly jobs by arrival order. The pairing does not affect the outcome:
both roles are confirmed either way.

_reading_the_timestamps: A record's `updated` field is the batch APPROVAL time for every job that submitted
successfully, because the confirmed path archives the file without saving it again.
All nine of the 2026-08-27 successes therefore read 07:58:46. Only a held record
carries a meaningful `updated`, since `hold()` does save.
So a successful job leaves no timestamp of its own, and you place it by the gap it
occupies between two holds. The confirmation emails line up with those gaps:
Replit at 07:59:01 before the first hold, Notion and Baseten inside 08:06:30-08:09:23,
Notion Developer Platform inside 08:09:59-08:10:54, and Harvey inside 08:12:53-08:14:37.
